about: Adaptive simulated SAT students (15-17) for the linear-equations mission. Same card format and how_to_use rules as tests/fixtures/students/a_tri.json (bank_keys, bursts, patience, ui_action_vocab). Pip opens with its misconception claim: 'When you move a number to the other side it stays the same, so 2x + 6 = 20 becomes 2x = 20 + 6 and x = 13.' Quiz: q_k1 take 6 off only the left of 2x + 6 = 20, still equal?; q_k2 solve 3x + 4 = 19; q_k3 is x = 4 a solution of 5x - 3 = 17? All lines are original.

personas.who: Gets every one right with 'change sides change signs'; fast, but has never thought about why the sign changes.
personas.style: lowercase, terse, equations inline with no spaces, 'bro', 'lowkey'

asks_why: bc when u switch sides the sign changes
idk thats just the rule. change sides change signs
oh wait its bc ur really subtracting 6 from both sides. the +6 and -6 cancel on the left
pip_wrong_prediction: no bro the 3 is multiplying, u divide
nudge_hint: ohh like a seesaw. if one kid gets off u gotta take the same off the other side
after_quiz_miss: nah u cant just move it. moving it is subtracting from both sides so 19-4 = 15 then x = 5
and 3 times 5 plus 4 is 19 so it checks

misconception.label: Sign-flip rule with no balance reason; becomes 'just move it' under speed
misconception.when: second text, as the reason. Not wrong, but it is a procedure with no reason; a good Pip asks for the why once, through a concrete case.

personas.knows_note: k1 (balance) only after a seesaw/scale nudge or a 'what if i take 6 off one side only' case.

expect.watch_for: 'change sides change signs' is a rule, not a reason; Pip may test it on a weird case (x/2 = 3, does the 2 flip to -2?) instead of asking 'but why?'.

expect.watch_for: She catches her own error on a check ('14 not 20'). Pip should let her notice, not announce it.
